title: Compiler-development evidence foundation
objective: Implement strict versioned evidence schemas, canonical SHA-256 identities, reason-code registry, validators, and adversarial fixtures for the compiler-development engine

oracles: Canonical JSON golden fixtures and adversarial mutation/stale-identity corpus

handoff.summary: Implemented immutable canonical JSON/SHA-256 identities, a reviewed stable reason registry, fail-closed validators and wire schemas for workloads, catalogs, profile receipts, overlays, dossiers, campaigns, and promotion receipts, evaluator telemetry trust boundaries, canonical cross-component compiler identity inputs, and golden/adversarial regression tests.
risks: The isolated scratch worktree initially lacked generated FLINT files; after supplying the matching adapter and generated manifest, all 15 active compiler fixtures passed.
The pure JavaScript validators were exercised on linux-x64 in this lane; integration still owns the required linux-arm64, windows-x64, and macos-arm64 validation matrix.

Consumers must use canonicalCompilerIdentity instead of retaining local source, artifact, or optimizer-catalog digest projections, and promotion callers must supply the complete trusted validatedInputs context.
next_steps: Replace dashboard, workload, and profiler compiler-identity adapters with canonicalCompilerIdentity and assert the shared implementation fields agree.
Run the portable validator suite on the required linux-arm64, windows-x64, and macos-arm64 matrix.
Require promotion integration to populate validatedInputs from already-validated receipts rather than raw candidate strings.
